title: Order pricing and partial refunds in integer cents
name: Order refund calculator

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code computes money amounts for orders and refunds? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
Why does priceOrder distribute the discount and tax across lines with allocate instead of rounding each line's share?
choices: The per-line parts must add up to exactly the order-level discount and tax, which independent rounding does not guarantee
Math.round is not available for numbers above 2^31
allocate converts cents to floating-point dollars for display
It guarantees that every line receives an equal share

questions.prompt: A refund request fails on the network after the gateway actually processed it, and the client retries the same request. Why is the customer not refunded twice?
choices: planRefund throws because the refunded quantity was already updated
The gateway rejects any refund smaller than the captured amount
The idempotency key is derived from the order id and the number of refunds already recorded, so the retry sends the same key and the gateway can deduplicate it
store.recordRefund is called before gateway.refund so the retry sees it

questions.prompt: Which input makes planRefund throw before any money moves?
choices: Refunding fewer units of a line than remain, after an earlier partial refund of that line
Refunding an order that has a discount applied
Requesting a quantity of exactly the original line quantity
Requesting more units of a SKU than have been bought and not yet refunded
